Part 2 · At the device

What does the operator do at a device, and what is kept?

Part 2 · the plan

From a close-up to a log line

  1. Read, check, operatethree actions, one log line each
  2. Gauge or transmitterwhich one shows the process
  3. Reading a hand valvestem, lever, seal
  4. Sixteen hand valvesnormal position and lock

At the device

Three actions, each written to the event log

◀ Read

A gauge or transmitter: the value and its unit.

◀ Check

A pump or control valve: running, stopped, open, closed.

◀ Operate

A hand valve: open or close it on the running plant.

So each action leaves a line of type FIELD in the event log.

Visual plant 3D · close-up

A close-up puts the dial at reading distance

PG-104, section 1 discharge, read from P5

  • Dial range 0–80 barg.
  • The transmitter display behind it shows the same loop.
  • Arriving in the close-up writes the Read line.

Interactive · build a log line

The log line is the evidence the grader reads

A gauge and its transmitter share one loop key, so either reading counts for that loop.

Interactive · a transmitter error

The gauge reads the process; the transmitter, the DCS signal

Accepted error$\delta=\max\left(0.02\,|v|,\ a\right)$

A gap wider than δ between gauge and display is a finding: the instrument, not the process.

Interactive · type and position

A hand valve shows its position; the DCS does not

Stem out or lever along the pipe means open; handwheel colour means nothing.

Interactive · pick a hand valve

Sixteen hand valves: eight operable, eight sealed

The register gives the normal position; only the field shows the actual one.

Locked and car-sealed

A round confirms the seal and never moves it

MV-146, block upstream of anti-surge valve UV-103; seal on the handwheel

LO, CSO

Blocks in a protection path: recycle, relief inlet, blowdown outlet.

LC

Drains and blinded vents kept shut.

◀ Operate refuses: breaking a seal needs a permit.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Read, check and operate each write a FIELD line.
  • Gauge and transmitter share one loop key.
  • A gap wider than δ between them is a finding.
  • Stem out or lever along the pipe: open.
  • Eight sealed valves are never moved on a round.

Visual plant 3D · rounds sheet

The sheet follows the walk, row by row

First seven rows, trainee view: the tag button walks to its station

Interactive · kind and station

Interactive · boxes named correctly

90 % means 24 boxes out of 26

Identify score$\text{score}=\dfrac{\text{correct}}{26}\ \geq\ 0.90$

Two misses still pass; a third drops the score to 88 %.

Interactive · pick an exercise

Eight exercises built on the round

Each is graded out of 10 at the first check; later checks show marks but keep the grade.

Exercises · field check

Training exercises carry a five-item field check

Five items

In round order, out of 5.

From the log

Ticks only from FIELD lines.

No cause named

Upset area mixed with ordinary items.

So the round tests the habit of going out, not a guess.

Interactive · where the answer came from

The console earns half; the field earns full

Six field checks and four console answers give 8 of 10: going to the device pays.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • The rounds sheet has 28 rows in walking order.
  • Identify passes at 24 of 26 boxes.
  • Field checks tick only from FIELD log lines.
  • A right answer from the console earns half.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Walk the 14 stations in order; the round is 314 m.

2

Read gauge and display together; a gap is a finding.

3

Judge a hand valve by stem or lever, never by colour.

4

Confirm every seal; never move a sealed valve on a round.

5

Go to the device: only a field line earns full credit.
